comments.author: greptile
comments.body:
**Mine initializes KG before lease**

When `mempalace_mine` first opens a knowledge graph, its caller evaluates `_get_kg(create=True)` before this code acquires the write lease. That can create the KG or adopt legacy facts even if another writer holds the lease and the mine returns “palace busy” with “Nothing was written.” It can also create a KG for a no-op mine. Initialize the KG only when the leased mine needs it.
comments.title: Mine initializes KG before lease

comments.author: greptile
comments.body:
**Unopenable table appears retryable**

If a cached drawer read fails and the fresh read-only open cannot open the table, the fresh handle has no table, but `count_by_pair` returns `{}` without raising. This code then tells the client the palace changed and to retry, even though the table remains unopenable and may need repair. Check that the fresh handle opened a table before giving the retry hint.
comments.title: Unopenable table appears retryable

comments.author: greptile
comments.body:
**Cached KG skips palace check**

If an operator removes the palace after an MCP session has used a KG tool, later KG calls reuse `_kg` without checking whether the palace still exists. They attempt SQLite access and return a generic internal tool error instead of the intended no-palace response with recovery guidance. Check the palace path on cached KG access too.
comments.title: Cached KG skips palace check
